outcome: need for packed red blood cell transfusion
cohort: The study included 19,446 women who underwent vaginal delivery, elective cesarean section, and urgent cesarean section at Carmel Medical Center from 2015 to 2020, excluding those with primary postpartum hemorrhage.
finding: Routine postoperative hemoglobin testing following elective cesarean section in asymptomatic patients without primary postpartum hemorrhage appears unnecessary.
mod_finding: Urgent cesarean section was associated with a higher risk of blood transfusion, but there was no significant difference between elective cesarean section and vaginal delivery in transfusion rates, and elective cesarean section had the lowest rates of post-delivery hemoglobin below 7 g/dL.
